facts.quote: An additional two new buildings were constructed, featuring designs inspired by the site's historic brickwork.

facts.fact: It reopened on 29 May 2018 as Tai Kwun, a centre for heritage and arts.
facts.quote: Surrounded by Hollywood Road, Arbuthnot Road, Chancery Lane, and Old Bailey Street, the compound underwent a heritage revitalisation and reopened to the public on 29 May 2018 as Tai Kwun (Chinese: 大館), a centre for heritage and arts.

facts.fact: In 2019 it received an award of excellence from the UNESCO Asia-Pacific Awards for Cultural Heritage Conservation.
facts.quote: In 2019, Tai Kwun received an award of excellence from the UNESCO Asia-Pacific Awards for Cultural Heritage Conservation.

facts.fact: The Yongnyongjon Hall of Jongmyo in Seoul is an example of the wing-like bracket form that appeared in the mid-Joseon period.
facts.quote: In the mid-Joseon period, the winglike bracket form appeared (an example is the Yongnyongjon Hall of Jongmyo, Seoul), which, according to some authors, better suited the peninsula's poor economic situation that resulted from repetitive invasions.

facts.fact: Menara Mesiniaga is a high-tech office building in Subang Jaya, Selangor, Malaysia.
facts.quote: Mesiniaga Tower or Menara Mesiniaga is a high-tech architectural building in SS16, Subang Jaya, Selangor, Malaysia.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1989 and was completed in 1992.
facts.quote: The building's construction began in 1989 and was completed in 1992.

facts.fact: In 1995 its architect, Ken Yeang, received the Aga Khan Award for Architecture.
facts.quote: In 1995, architect Ken Yeang, who designed the building, was awarded with the Aga Khan Award for Architecture.

facts.fact: Built for IBM, it uses a shaded facade, recessed terraces, a rooftop pool and planting on the outside.
facts.quote: The Mesiniaga Tower (1992), an office building for IBM in Subang Jaya, Malaysia, incorporated strategies such as a shaded façade, recessed terraces, a rooftop pool, and a vegetated exterior.

facts.fact: It is a climate-responsive tower that shows Yeang's principles of the 'bioclimatic skyscraper'.
facts.quote: Menara Mesiniaga Tower – Selangor, Malaysia (1992) – a climate-responsive tower that exemplifies Yeang’s key principles for 'bioclimatic skyscraper' design, and received the Aga Khan Award for Architecture, the RAIA (Royal Australian Institute of Architects) International Award, the Malaysian institute of Architects Design Award.

facts.fact: Rose Seidler House is a heritage-listed former home, now a house museum, in Wahroonga, a Sydney suburb.
facts.quote: Rose Seidler House is a heritage-listed former residence and now house museum located at 69–71 Clissold Road in the Sydney suburb of Wahroonga in the Ku-ring-gai Council local government area of New South Wales, Australia.

facts.fact: Harry Seidler designed it, and it was built from 1948 to 1950.
facts.quote: It was designed by Harry Seidler and built from 1948 to 1950 by Bret R. Lake.

facts.fact: It was designed for Seidler's parents and named after his mother Rose, who drove the commission.
facts.quote: The mid-century modern house was designed for both of Seidler's parents – Rose and Max Seidler, however since Rose Seidler was the person who initiated and drove the commission, making all the main client decisions, the house is named after only her.

facts.fact: It is built of four basic materials: natural bush stone, reinforced concrete, timber and glass.
facts.quote: The house is constructed of four basic materials; natural bush stone, reinforced concrete, timber and glass.

facts.fact: Built in the International modernist style, it was futuristic for Australia at the time and is an outstanding example of mid-century modern houses.
facts.quote: Built in 1949–1950 in the International modernist style, it was futuristic and modern for Australia at that time, and is an outstanding example of mid-century-modern domestic architecture.

facts.fact: Every room except the main bathroom has a full view, bringing the outside in.
facts.quote: Each room except the main bathroom has a full view, bringing the outside, inside.

facts.fact: Its bi-nuclear plan separates living areas from bedrooms, linked by a playroom and deck.
facts.quote: The bi-nuclear plan clearly separates living areas from sleeping and bathrooms. These are connected by the flexible transitional zones of the playroom and deck.

facts.fact: It was added to the New South Wales State Heritage Register on 2 April 1999.
facts.quote: It was added to the New South Wales State Heritage Register on 2 April 1999.

facts.fact: The Shine Dome is a Canberra landmark known for its unusual structure, nicknamed "The Martian Embassy" for its shape.
facts.quote: The Shine Dome (previously known as Becker House) is a well-known Canberra landmark, notable for its unusual structure, and colloquially referred to as "The Martian Embassy", an allusion to its shape and the fact that as the capital of Australia, Canberra is the home of foreign embassies.

facts.fact: It houses the secretariat of the Australian Academy of Science.
facts.quote: The Academy Secretariat is in Canberra, at the Shine Dome.

facts.fact: It was designed by Sir Roy Grounds, of Grounds, Romberg and Boyd.
facts.quote: It was designed by architect Sir Roy Grounds, of Grounds, Romberg and Boyd.

facts.fact: When completed in 1959, its 45.75-metre dome was the largest in Australia.
facts.quote: When completed in 1959 its 45.75-metre-diameter dome was the largest in Australia.

facts.fact: It is a 710-tonne reinforced concrete dome on 16 thin supports.
facts.quote: The plan accepted involved a 710-tonne reinforced concrete dome, which had to be supported by 16 thin supports.

facts.fact: The concrete is about 60 cm thick at the supports and 10 cm at the top, and the dome holds itself up with no internal walls.
facts.quote: The concrete is approximately 60 cm thick at the base supports, and 10 cm at the top. The dome supports itself, with no internal wall holding it up.

facts.fact: Building its reinforced concrete dome was a considerable technical achievement.
facts.quote: The construction of its reinforced concrete dome was a considerable technical achievement.

facts.fact: In 2000 it was renamed after the Fellow John Shine, who gave one million dollars to renovate the dome.
facts.quote: In 2000, it was renamed in honour of Fellow John Shine, who donated one million dollars to renovate the dome.

facts.fact: Federation Square is a venue for arts, culture and public events on the edge of Melbourne's central business district.
facts.quote: Federation Square (marketed and colloquially known as Fed Square) is a venue for arts, culture and public events on the edge of the Melbourne central business district.

facts.fact: It covers 3.2 hectares at Flinders and Swanston Streets, built over busy railway lines.
facts.quote: It covers an area of 3.2 ha (7.9 acres) at the intersection of Flinders and Swanston Streets built above busy railway lines and across the road from Flinders Street station.

facts.fact: A team led by Lab Architecture Studio (Donald Bates and Peter Davidson), with Bates Smart as local architects, won the design competition in July 1997.
facts.quote: The winner announced on 28 July 1997, a consortium led by Lab Architecture Studio directed by Donald Bates and Peter Davidson from London, with the Dutch landscape architects Karres en Brands, directed by Sylvia Karres and Bart Brands, teamed with local executive architects Bates Smart for the second stage.

facts.fact: The design is complex and irregular, with angled 'cranked' geometries in both plan and facades.
facts.quote: The design, originally costed at between $110 and $150 million, was complex and irregular, with gently angled 'cranked' geometries predominating in both the planning and the facade treatment of the various buildings and the wintergardens that surrounded and defined the open spaces.

facts.fact: The cladding mixes zinc, perforated zinc, glass, frosted glass and sandstone in a camouflage-like pinwheel tiling.
facts.quote: The cladding is composed of 6 different materials, zinc, perforated zinc, glass, frosted glass, sandstone and no cladding, in a camouflage-like pattern, and created using pinwheel tiling.

facts.fact: The main square is paved in 470,000 ochre sandstone blocks from Western Australia.
facts.quote: While bluestone is used for the majority of the paving in the Atrium and St Paul's Court, matching footpaths elsewhere in central Melbourne, the main square is paved in 470,000 ochre-coloured sandstone blocks from Western Australia and invokes images of the outback.

facts.fact: A "labyrinth" under the square, above the railway lines, cools the buildings passively.
facts.quote: The "labyrinth" is a passive cooling system sandwiched above the railway lines and below the middle of the square.

facts.fact: The square opened on 26 October 2002.
facts.quote: The square was opened on 26 October 2002.

facts.fact: The Royal National Theatre on London's South Bank, by Denys Lasdun, is Grade II* listed and one of the most notable Brutalist buildings in the UK.
facts.quote: Hailed as "the greatest English architect of the early heroic modern period", his most known work is the Royal National Theatre, on London's South Bank of the Thames, which is a Grade II* listed building and one of the most notable examples of Brutalist design in the United Kingdom.

facts.fact: The building holds three separate theatres.
facts.quote: The National Theatre building houses three separate theatres.

facts.fact: The main auditorium, the Olivier, is modelled on the ancient theatre at Epidaurus, with an open stage and fan-shaped seating for 1,160.
facts.quote: Named after the theatre's first artistic director, Laurence Olivier, this is the main auditorium. Modelled on the Ancient Theatre of Epidaurus, it has an open stage and a fan-shaped audience seating area for 1160 people.

facts.fact: It is built mainly of pale concrete, chosen to match the stone of Waterloo Bridge and Somerset House.
facts.quote: The building's main construction material is a pale concrete, intended to complement the colour of the stone of Waterloo Bridge and Somerset House.

facts.fact: The concrete was cast in rough timber formwork, leaving the wood grain visible inside and out.
facts.quote: The concrete was cast in formwork made from rough wooden planks, and the imprint of the wood was left in place so that it is visible on the building's internal and external surfaces.

facts.fact: At its opening the historian Mark Girouard called its style "an aesthetic of broken forms".
facts.quote: The style of the National Theatre building was described by architecture historian Mark Girouard as "an aesthetic of broken forms" at the time of opening.

facts.fact: In 1988 the future Charles III called it "a clever way of building a nuclear power station in the middle of London without anyone objecting".
facts.quote: Most notoriously, the future Charles III described the building in 1988 as "a clever way of building a nuclear power station in the middle of London without anyone objecting".

facts.fact: Despite the controversy, it has been Grade II* listed since 1994.
facts.quote: Despite controversy about its design, the theatre has been a Grade II* listed building since 1994.

facts.fact: The Sainsbury Centre is an art museum on the University of East Anglia campus in Norwich.
facts.quote: The Sainsbury Centre is an art museum located on the campus of the University of East Anglia, Norwich, England.

facts.fact: It was one of the first major public buildings by Norman Foster and Wendy Cheesman, completed in 1978.
facts.quote: The building, which contains a collection of world art, was one of the first major public buildings to be designed by the architects Norman Foster and Wendy Cheesman, completed in 1978.

facts.fact: It puts every function inside one flexible enclosure, a 'universal space' designed to allow for change.
facts.quote: According to Chris Abel, the building exemplifies Foster's early work of "a regular structure embracing all functions within a single, flexible enclosure, or 'universal space'" where "the design is all about allowing for change, internally and externally."

facts.fact: It is a large clad steel box on sloping grass.
facts.quote: The main building is sited on sloping, turfed ground, and consists of a large cuboid, clad steel structure.

facts.fact: One end is almost fully glazed, showing the prefabricated frame, and inside is one vast open space with no divisions.
facts.quote: One face is almost entirely glazed, with the prefabricated skeleton clearly visible. Internally, the museum gives the impression of being one vast open space, lacking any internal divisions to interfere with the interplay of natural and artificial light.

facts.fact: Services, lighting and toilets sit in triangular towers and trusses, between the outer cladding and inner aluminium louvres.
facts.quote: Services, lighting, toilets and maintenance access are housed in triangular towers and trusses, and between the external cladding and internal aluminium louvres.

facts.fact: A later basement extension opens through a curved glass front onto a man-made lake.
facts.quote: The sloping site allowed for an enlarged basement to emerge at a curved glass frontage overlooking a man-made lake (an echo of the nearby 13th-century Norfolk Broads).

facts.fact: It became Grade II* listed in December 2012.
facts.quote: The building became Grade II* listed in December 2012.

facts.fact: The Isokon building in Belsize Park, London, is a reinforced concrete block of flats designed by Wells Coates for Molly and Jack Pritchard.
facts.quote: Isokon Flats, also known as Lawn Road Flats and the Isokon building, on Lawn Road, Belsize Park in the London Borough of Camden, is a reinforced-concrete block of 36 flats (originally 32), designed by Canadian engineer Wells Coates for Molly and Jack Pritchard.

facts.fact: It opened on 9 July 1934 as an experiment in minimal city living.
facts.quote: Designs for the flats were developed between 1929–1932 and the complex opened on 9 July 1934 as an experiment in minimalist urban living.

facts.fact: The flats had very small kitchens, because a shared kitchen sent meals up by dumbwaiter.
facts.quote: All of the "Existenzminimum" flats had very small kitchens as there was a communal kitchen for the preparation of meals, connected to the residential floors via a dumbwaiter.

facts.fact: Residents included the Bauhaus émigrés Walter Gropius, Marcel Breuer and László Moholy-Nagy, and the writer Agatha Christie.
facts.quote: Celebrated residents included: Bauhaus émigrés Walter Gropius, Marcel Breuer, and László Moholy-Nagy; architects Egon Riss and Arthur Korn; writer Agatha Christie (between 1941 and 1947) and her husband Max Mallowan, art historian Adrian Stokes, the author Nicholas Monsarrat, the archaeologist V. Gordon Childe, modernist architect Jacques Groag and his wife, textile designer Jacqueline Groag.

facts.fact: Its simple living spaces were strongly influenced by Coates's Japanese upbringing and had built-in Isokon furniture.
facts.quote: With simple living spaces strongly influenced by Coates' Japanese experience, and including built-in Isokon furniture, Isokon was "an experiment in collective housing designed for left-wing intellectuals".

facts.fact: Avanti Architects restored it in 2003.
facts.quote: In 2003 the building was sympathetically refurbished by Avanti Architects, a practice which specialises in the renovation of modernist buildings, for the Notting Hill Housing Association which purchased it from Camden London Borough Council.

facts.fact: Its exterior is the palest pink, as it was originally, not pure white as black-and-white photos suggested.
facts.quote: The building now has a smooth external finish and is the palest tint of pink in colour, as it was originally—not pure white as has been assumed from black and white historical photos.

facts.fact: It was Grade I listed in 1999.
facts.quote: The building was designated a Grade I listed structure in 1999, placing it amongst the most significant historic buildings in England.

facts.fact: Sir John Soane's Museum is a house museum by Lincoln's Inn Fields in London, once the home of the neoclassical architect John Soane.
facts.quote: Sir John Soane's Museum is a house museum, located next to Lincoln's Inn Fields in Holborn, London, which was formerly the home of neo-classical architect John Soane.

facts.fact: It holds drawings and models of Soane's projects and his large collection of paintings, sculptures and antiquities.
facts.quote: It holds many drawings and architectural models of Soane's projects and a large collection of paintings, sculptures, drawings, and antiquities that he acquired over many years.

facts.fact: By an Act of Parliament, the house and collections passed to trustees for the nation on Soane's death, to be kept as nearly as possible as he left them.
facts.quote: The act stipulated that on Soane's death, his house and collections would pass into the care of a board of trustees acting on behalf of the nation, and that they would be preserved as nearly as possible exactly in the state they were at his death.

facts.fact: Soane bought No. 13, today the museum, and rebuilt it in two phases in 1808–09 and 1812.
facts.quote: After becoming Professor of Architecture at the Royal Academy in 1806, Soane purchased No. 13, the house next door, today the museum, and rebuilt it in two phases in 1808–09 and 1812.

facts.fact: He then treated the building as an architectural laboratory, constantly remodelling the interiors.
facts.quote: After completing No.13, Soane set about treating the building as an architectural laboratory, continually remodelling the interiors.

facts.fact: Its most famous spaces are at the back: the dome area, the colonnade and the museum corridor.
facts.quote: The most famous spaces in the house are those at the rear of the museum – the dome area, colonnade and museum corridor.

facts.fact: These are mostly lit from above, a small-scale version of the lighting Soane devised for the banking halls of the Bank of England.
facts.quote: These are mostly toplit and provide some idea in miniature form of the ingenious lighting contrived by Soane for the toplit banking halls at the Bank of England.

facts.fact: The domed ceiling of the Breakfast Room, set with convex mirrors, has influenced architects worldwide.
facts.quote: The domed ceiling of the Breakfast Room, inset with convex mirrors, has influenced architects from around the world.

facts.fact: The collection includes over 30,000 architectural drawings and the Sarcophagus of Seti I.
facts.quote: There are over 30,000 architectural drawings in the collection, along with various Egyptian, Greek and Roman antiquities, including the Sarcophagus of Seti I.

facts.fact: The Fondation Cartier is a centre for contemporary art set up by Cartier in 1984.
facts.quote: The Fondation Cartier was created in 1984 by the Cartier SA firm as a center for contemporary art that presents exhibits by established artists, offers young artists a chance to debut, and incorporates works into its collection.

facts.fact: In 1994 it moved to a glass building by Jean Nouvel at 261 Boulevard Raspail, Paris, set in a woodland garden by Lothar Baumgarten.
facts.quote: In 1994, it moved to a glass building at 261 Boulevard Raspail designed by Pritzker Prize architect Jean Nouvel on the site of the former American Center for Students and Artists, surrounded by a modern woodland garden landscaped by Lothar Baumgarten.

facts.fact: The ground floor is eight metres high and glazed on all sides.
facts.quote: The ground floor of the building is eight meters (26 feet) high and glassed in on all sides.

facts.fact: In 2014 the foundation commissioned Nouvel to work on expanding the Boulevard Raspail building.
facts.quote: By 2014, the foundation abandoned plans to relocate to the island and instead commissioned Nouvel to work on the expansion of the Boulevard Raspail premises.

facts.fact: The foundation stayed at Boulevard Raspail until 2025, when it moved to the Palais-Royal area.
facts.quote: It was located at 261 Boulevard Raspail in the 14th arrondissement of Paris until 2025, when it relocated to the Palais-Royal area, reopening to the public on 25 October 2025.

facts.fact: The Millau Viaduct is a multi-span cable-stayed bridge, completed in 2004, across the Tarn valley near Millau in southern France.
facts.quote: The Millau Viaduct (French: Viaduc de Millau [vja.dyk də mi.jo]) is a multispan cable-stayed bridge completed in 2004 across the gorge valley of the Tarn near (west of) Millau in the Aveyron department in the Occitanie Region, in Southern France.

facts.fact: The design team was led by the engineer Michel Virlogeux and the architect Norman Foster.
facts.quote: The design team was led by engineer Michel Virlogeux and English architect Norman Foster.

facts.fact: It was the world's tallest bridge for over two decades, with a structural height of 343 metres.
facts.quote: It was the tallest bridge in the world for over two decades (until late 2025), with a structural height of 343 metres (1,125 ft).

facts.fact: It was built in three years and opened in December 2004.
facts.quote: It was built over three years, formally inaugurated on 14 December 2004, and opened to traffic two days later on 16 December.

facts.fact: After wind tunnel tests, the shape of the road deck was changed and the pylon design refined.
facts.quote: After undergoing wind tunnel tests, the shape of the road deck was altered, and detailed corrections were made to the design of the pylons.

facts.fact: The road deck was built on the plateaus at each end and pushed out over the pylons.
facts.quote: The bridge road deck was constructed on plateaus at both ends of the viaduct, and pushed onto the pylons using bridge launching techniques.

facts.fact: It is ranked among the great engineering achievements of modern times and won IABSE's 2006 Outstanding Structure Award.
facts.quote: The bridge has been consistently ranked as one of the greatest engineering achievements of modern times, and received the 2006 Outstanding Structure Award from the International Association for Bridge and Structural Engineering.

facts.fact: The Pavillon Le Corbusier is an art museum in Zürich dedicated to the work of Le Corbusier.
facts.quote: The Pavillon Le Corbusier is a Swiss art museum in Zürich-Seefeld at Zürichhorn dedicated to the work of the French-Swiss architect Le Corbusier.

facts.fact: It is Le Corbusier's last building, and marks a break from his concrete and stone towards steel and glass.
facts.quote: It is the last building designed by Le Corbusier marking a radical change of his achievement of using concrete and stone, framed in steel and glass, in the 1960s created as a signpost for the future.

facts.fact: It uses prefabricated steel parts with multi-coloured enamelled panels, under a 'free-floating' roof that shelters the house from rain and sun.
facts.quote: Le Corbusier made intensive use of prefabricated steel elements combined with multi-coloured enamelled plates fitted to the central core, and above the complex he designed a 'free-floating' roof to keep the house protected from the rain and the sun.

facts.fact: The steel roof was prefabricated, assembled on the ground, then lifted by crane to its height of 9 metres.
facts.quote: The roof was prefabricated and thereafter, in the biggest possible units, transported to the building site, where it was assembled on the ground. The two finally welded parts of the roof were then lifted to their final height (9 metres (30 ft)) by a crane and fixed on the pillars.

facts.fact: The frame is made of 2.26-metre cubes, with walls, windows, ceilings and floors screwed onto it.
facts.quote: It consists of cubes 2.26 x 2.26 metres (7.4 ft) which were assembled on the site. Walls, windows, ceilings and floors were then screwed onto the steel frame.

facts.fact: The first design was in concrete, but in 1962 it was changed to a steel building.
facts.quote: One year later, the first drawings for a building to be constructed in concrete were presented, and in 1962 the concept was changed to a steel building.

facts.fact: Le Corbusier died in 1965, and the building opened on 15 July 1967.
facts.quote: In 1965, Le Corbusier died. On 15 July 1967, the Centre Le Corbusier was officially inaugurated.

facts.fact: It is listed as a Swiss cultural property of national importance.
facts.quote: The museum is listed in the Swiss inventory of cultural property of national and regional significance as a Class A object of national importance.

facts.fact: Park Güell is a complex of parks and gardens with architectural elements in the Gràcia district of Barcelona.
facts.quote: Park Güell (Catalan: Parc Güell [ˈpaɾɡ ˈɡweʎ]; Spanish: Parque Güell) is a complex of parks and gardens in Barcelona with architectural elements, located in the La Salut neighborhood of the Gràcia district in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.

facts.fact: The industrialist Eusebi Güell commissioned Antoni Gaudí to design it.
facts.quote: In the context of Barcelona's late 19th and early 20th-century urban expansion, Catalan industrialist and art patron Eusebi Güell commissioned architect Antoni Gaudí, a leading figure of the aesthetic movement in Catalan modernism, to design a park.

facts.fact: It was built between 1900 and 1914 and opened to the public in 1926.
facts.quote: Construction took place between 1900 and 1914, and the park officially opened to the public in 1926.

facts.fact: Güell first planned it as a high-end housing estate inspired by the English garden city movement.
facts.quote: Count Eusebi Güell had originally planned to establish a high-end residential development for the bourgeoisie, inspired by the English garden city movement.

facts.fact: Its focal point is a terrace edged by a long curving bench like a sea serpent, designed by Josep Maria Jujol.
facts.quote: The park's focal point is a terrace bordered by a long, curving bench shaped like a sea serpent. Designed by Josep Maria Jujol, the bench’s ergonomic form creates enclaves to encourage social interaction.

facts.fact: Gaudí built the raised paths from local stone, with columns and vaults that imitate tree trunks.
facts.quote: Designed by Gaudí using local stone, they blend seamlessly with the landscape. Their columns and vaulted supports mimic tree trunks and natural forms.

facts.fact: He used inverted catenary arches so the structure works in compression.
facts.quote: As with his earlier work at Colònia Güell, Gaudí used inverted catenary arches to achieve optimal load-bearing compression.

facts.fact: Since 1984 it has been part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Works of Antoni Gaudí".
facts.quote: In 1984, UNESCO designated the park a World Heritage Site, recognizing it as part of the "Works of Antoni Gaudí" collection and stating "the architecture of the park combined elements from the Arts and Crafts movement, Symbolism, Expressionism, and Rationalism, and presaged and influenced many forms and techniques of 20th-century Modernism."

facts.fact: Igualada Cemetery, near Barcelona, was designed by Enric Miralles and Carme Pinós after they won a competition in 1984.
facts.quote: Igualada Cemetery or New Cemetery (Catalan: Cementiri Nou) is a cemetery in Igualada, near Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain, designed by the architects Enric Miralles and Carme Pinós after winning an architectural competition in 1984.

facts.fact: Built between 1985 and 1994, it is widely regarded as one of the most poetic works of 20th-century Catalan architecture.
facts.quote: Constructed between 1985 and 1994 as a replacement for the Old Cemetery (Catalan: "Cementiri Vell"), the cemetery became widely regarded as one of the most poetic works of twentieth century Catalan architecture.

facts.fact: The architects set out to explore the cycle of life, linking past, present and future.
facts.quote: Miralles and Pinós were concerned, not just to design a cemetery, but to explore poetic ideas regarding the acceptance of the cycle of life to enable a link between the past, the present, and the future.

facts.fact: It is conceived partly as an earthwork that reshapes the landscape and partly as a metaphor for the river of life.
facts.quote: The project is conceived, in part, as an earthwork that transforms the surrounding landscape and also, in part, as a metaphor for the river of life.

facts.fact: A processional 'street' descends from the entrance, where crossed rusting steel poles serve as gates.
facts.quote: A processional "street" descends from the entrance, where crossed, rusting, steel poles doubling as gates and likened to the crosses at Calvary, proclaim the start of a winding pathway towards the burial area.

facts.fact: The route is lined with concrete burial niches that act as retaining walls, and railway sleepers are set into the concrete path.
facts.quote: The route is lined with repeatable concrete loculi forming retaining walls and the floor of the path has railway sleepers set into its concrete surface.

facts.fact: The aim was to bring mourners down into the landscape, to a 'city of the dead' where the dead and the living come closer.
facts.quote: The intention was to bring the bereaved down into the landscape to a 'city of the dead', an in between place where the dead and the living are brought closer together.

facts.fact: Enric Miralles, who died in 2000, is buried there.
facts.quote: Enric Miralles, who died in the year 2000 is buried in one of the tombs.

facts.fact: The Colegio Nuestra Señora de las Maravillas is a private Catholic La Salle school in Madrid.
facts.quote: Colegio Nuestra Señora de las Maravillas (English:Our Lady of Wonders) is a private Catholic school in Madrid, Spain, belonging to the order of La Salle founded in 1892 by Brother Justinus Marie, belonging to the Brothers of the Christian Schools of La Salle.

facts.fact: Its gymnasium opened in 1962 and is considered one of Madrid's great buildings, studied by architecture students.
facts.quote: In 1962, the gymnasium was inaugurated, considered today as one of the greatest architectural constructions of Madrid, and is being studied by architecture students.

facts.fact: Alejandro de la Sota designed it to bridge a 12-metre drop between Guadalquivir and Joaquín Costa streets.
facts.quote: was designed and built by the architect Alejandro de la Sota required to bridge a gap of 12 meters between the Guadalquivir and Joaquín Costa streets.

facts.fact: Real Madrid's basketball team once played its home games in the gym.
facts.quote: The Gym, in addition to appearing in numerous publications for its architectural significance and prominence, was the court where the Real Madrid Basketball played their home games during the building of the Real Madrid Sports City and his Raimundo Saporta Pavilion.

facts.fact: The Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe in Berlin, designed by Peter Eisenman with Buro Happold, commemorates the Jewish victims of the Holocaust.
facts.quote: The Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe (German: Denkmal für die ermordeten Juden Europas), also known as the Holocaust Memorial (German: Holocaust-Mahnmal), is a memorial in Berlin to the Jewish victims of the Holocaust committed by Nazi Germany, designed by architect Peter Eisenman and Buro Happold.

facts.fact: It covers a 1.9-hectare site with 2,711 concrete slabs, or stelae, in a grid on sloping ground.
facts.quote: It consists of a 1.9-hectare (4.7-acre) site covered with 2,711 concrete slabs or "stelae", arranged in a grid pattern on a sloping field.

facts.fact: The stelae are 2.38 m long and 0.95 m wide, and range from 0.2 to 4.7 m high.
facts.quote: The stelae are 2.38 m (7 ft 9+1⁄2 in) long, 0.95 m (3 ft 1+1⁄2 in) wide and vary in height from 0.2 to 4.7 metres (8 in to 15 ft 5 in).

facts.fact: The grid leaves long, narrow, straight alleys between the blocks, and the ground undulates along them.
facts.quote: This allows for long, straight, and narrow alleys between them, along which the ground undulates.

facts.fact: An underground 'Place of Information' holds the names of about 3 million Jewish Holocaust victims, from Yad Vashem.
facts.quote: An attached underground "Place of Information" (German: Ort der Information) holds the names of approximately 3 million Jewish Holocaust victims, obtained from the Israeli museum Yad Vashem.

facts.fact: It was built from April 2003 to December 2004 and inaugurated on 10 May 2005, 60 years after the war ended in Europe.
facts.quote: Building began on 1 April 2003, and was finished on 15 December 2004. It was inaugurated on 10 May 2005, 60 years after the end of World War II in Europe, and opened to the public two days later.

facts.fact: It stands one block south of the Brandenburg Gate.
facts.quote: It is located one block south of the Brandenburg Gate, in the Mitte neighbourhood.

facts.fact: Eisenman wrote that the stelae should create an uneasy, confusing atmosphere, an ordered system that has lost touch with human reason.
facts.quote: According to Eisenman's project text, the stelae are designed to produce an uneasy, confusing atmosphere, and the whole sculpture aims to represent a supposedly ordered system that has lost touch with human reason.

facts.fact: The former Van Nelle Factory on the Schie in Rotterdam is a prime example of modernist and functionalist architecture.
facts.quote: The former Van Nelle Factory (Dutch: Van Nellefabriek) on the Schie in Rotterdam, is considered a prime example of the modernist and functionalist architecture.

facts.fact: Built from 1925 to 1931, it was designed by Leendert van der Vlugt of Brinkman & Van der Vlugt with the reinforced-concrete engineer J.G. Wiebenga.
facts.quote: Built between 1925 and 1931, the buildings were designed by architect Leendert van der Vlugt from the Brinkman & Van der Vlugt office in cooperation with civil engineer J.G. Wiebenga, at that time a specialist for constructions in reinforced concrete.

facts.fact: It is an example of Nieuwe Bouwen, Dutch modernist architecture.
facts.quote: It is an example of Nieuwe Bouwen, modernist architecture in the Netherlands.

facts.fact: It processed coffee, tea and tobacco through the 20th century.
facts.quote: In the 20th century, it was a factory, processing coffee, tea, and tobacco and, later on, also chewing gum, cigarettes, instant pudding, and rice.

facts.fact: Le Corbusier called it "the most beautiful spectacle of the modern age" in 1932.
facts.quote: Soon after it was built, prominent architects described the factory as "the most beautiful spectacle of the modern age" (Le Corbusier in 1932) and "a poem in steel and glass" (Robertson in 1930).

facts.fact: It is said to have had the world's first industrially prefabricated curtain wall.
facts.quote: It is claimed that the building featured the first industrially prefabricated curtain wall in the world.

facts.fact: For its change of use, Wessel de Jonge coordinated the renovation, which began in 2000.
facts.quote: Eric Gude, a Dutch specialist in the conversion of former industrial sites, planned and organized this change of use for the Van Nelle factory in 1997 and introduced Wessel de Jonge, an authority on the renovation of modern architecture in 1999, to coordinate the overall renovation, which began in the year 2000.

facts.fact: It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2014.
facts.quote: It has been a designated UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2014.

facts.fact: WoZoCo housing in Amsterdam (1994–1997) is one of MVRDV's early built works.
facts.quote: Other early built works include the Wozoco housing in Amsterdam (1994–1997) and the Dutch Pavilion at the Hannover World Exhibition Expo 2000 (1997–2000).

facts.fact: The Wozoco senior citizens' homes in Amsterdam won the A.J. van Eck Prize of the Dutch Architects' Association and helped make MVRDV internationally known.
facts.quote: The studies on light urbanism for the City of Rotterdam, the headquarters of the Dutch Public Broadcasting Company VPRO and the Wozoco's senior citizens' residences in Amsterdam, which won the A.J. van Eck Prize of the Dutch Architects' Association, have brought MVRDV to the attention of a vast collection of clients, giving the studio international renown.

facts.fact: The Chapel of Saint Benedict is a Roman Catholic chapel in Sumvitg, Graubünden, Switzerland.
facts.quote: The Chapel of Saint Benedict (Romansh: Caplutta Sogn Benedetg; German: Kapelle des Heiligen Benedikt) is a Roman Catholic church located in Sumvitg, Surselva Region, canton of Graubünden, Switzerland.

facts.fact: After a 1984 avalanche destroyed a Baroque chapel on the site, Disentis Abbey decided to build a new one.
facts.quote: After a 1984 avalanche destroyed a Baroque chapel on the same site, the Disentis Abbey decided to build a new chapel.

facts.fact: Peter Zumthor won the competition to design it.
facts.quote: Architect Peter Zumthor won the architectural competition for the project.

facts.fact: It was built between 1985 and 1989 for CHF 600,000.
facts.quote: The new chapel was built between 1985 and 1989 for a total cost of CHF 600,000.

facts.fact: The engineers were Jürg Buchli and Jürg Conzett.
facts.quote: Jürg Buchli and Jürg Conzett were the engineers.

facts.fact: The Fondation Beyeler's museum in Riehen, near Basel, houses the art collection of Hildy and Ernst Beyeler.
facts.quote: The Beyeler Foundation or Fondation Beyeler, with its museum in Riehen, near Basel (Switzerland), owns and oversees the art collection of Hildy and Ernst Beyeler, which features modern and traditional art.

facts.fact: The Beyelers set up the foundation in 1982 and commissioned Renzo Piano to design a museum for their collection.
facts.quote: Art dealers Ernst Beyeler (16 July 1921 – 25 February 2010) and Hilda Kunz (1922 – 18 July 2008), known as Hildy, created the Beyeler Foundation in 1982 and commissioned Renzo Piano to design a museum to house their private collection.

facts.fact: The museum opened on 18 October 1997, showing 140 works of modern classics.
facts.quote: The Beyeler Foundation opened its doors on 18 October 1997, presenting 140 works of modern classics, including 23 Picassos.

facts.fact: At the founder's request it was designed to feel tranquil, with white walls, pale wooden floors and natural light.
facts.quote: It was designed, at the request of the founder, to inspire tranquility, with white walls, light-colored wooden floors, and natural light.

facts.fact: Its glazed facade looks out over the cornfields and vines of the Tüllinger Hills.
facts.quote: The building features a glazed façade largely looking out onto the corn fields and vines covering the Tüllinger Hills.

facts.fact: Four 115-metre walls of Patagonian porphyry, running north to south 7 metres apart, set out the plan.
facts.quote: The four 115-metre (377 ft) long porphyry walls running from north to south and standing 7 metres (23 ft) apart define the plan of the building.

facts.fact: A light glass roof on the walls admits north light but screens east and west light, and overhangs far to shade the glass facades.
facts.quote: Resting on top of the solid foundation walls, the lightweight glass roof, white enamelled on the reverse, admits northern light but screens off light from the east and the west. Along the northern and the southern sides the roof projects far beyond the walls, shading the glass façades from the sun.

facts.fact: In 2026 the foundation completed an expansion by Peter Zumthor.
facts.quote: In 2026, the Fondation Beyeler completed an expansion by architect Peter Zumthor, selected in 2016 from a field of 100 architects, including Sou Fujimoto, Jun'ya Ishigami, Christian Kerez, Hiroshi Nakamura, Smiljan Radić Clarke, SANAA, Eduardo Souto de Moura and Tod Williams Billie Tsien Architects.

facts.fact: The Secession Building is a contemporary art exhibition hall in Vienna.
facts.quote: The Secession Building (German: Secessionsgebäude) is a contemporary art exhibition hall in Vienna, Austria.

facts.fact: Joseph Maria Olbrich completed it in 1898 as an architectural manifesto for the Vienna Secession, a group of rebel artists.
facts.quote: It was completed in 1898 by Joseph Maria Olbrich as an architectural manifesto for the Vienna Secession, a group of rebel artists that seceded from the long-established fine art institution.

facts.fact: It houses Gustav Klimt's Beethoven Frieze, one of the best-known works of the Secession style.
facts.quote: The building features the Beethoven Frieze by Gustav Klimt, one of the most widely recognized artworks of Secession style (a branch of Art Nouveau, also known as Jugendstil in Germany and Nordic countries).

facts.fact: It was financed by Karl Wittgenstein.
facts.quote: The building was financed by Karl Wittgenstein, the father of Ludwig Wittgenstein.

facts.fact: Above the entrance is the movement's motto: "To every age its art, to every art its freedom".
facts.quote: The motto of the Secessionist movement is written above the entrance of the pavilion: "To every age its art, to every art its freedom" (German: Der Zeit ihre Kunst. Der Kunst ihre Freiheit).

facts.fact: Below the motto, three gorgons stand for painting, sculpture and architecture.
facts.quote: Below this is a sculpture of three gorgons representing painting, sculpture, and architecture.

facts.fact: It became the landmark of the Secession movement.
facts.quote: Olbrich designed their exhibition building, the famous Secession Building, which became the movement's landmark.

facts.fact: It appears on the Austrian 50-cent euro coin.
facts.quote: The building has been selected to figure on the national side of the €0.50 Austrian coin.

facts.fact: Grundtvig's Church in Copenhagen's Bispebjerg district is a rare example of expressionist church architecture.
facts.quote: Grundtvig's Church (Danish: Grundtvigs Kirke) is located in the Bispebjerg district of Copenhagen, Denmark. It is a rare example of expressionist church architecture.

facts.fact: Peder Vilhelm Jensen-Klint won the design competition in 1913.
facts.quote: The commission for the construction of a church to be named after the Danish philosopher, pastor and hymn writer N. F. S. Grundtvig was decided through a competition, won by Peder Vilhelm Jensen-Klint in 1913.

facts.fact: Work continued until 1940 and was completed by his son Kaare Klint after his death in 1930.
facts.quote: Further work on the interior and on adjacent buildings continued until 1940 and was completed by Klint's son Kaare Klint after his father's death in 1930.

facts.fact: The architect studied many Danish village churches with stepped gables in preparation.
facts.quote: In preparation for the project, the architect studied many Danish village churches, particularly those on the island of Zealand with stepped gables.

facts.fact: It merges the geometric forms of Brick Expressionism with the verticality of Gothic architecture.
facts.quote: Klint merged the modern geometric forms of Brick Expressionism with the classical vertical of Gothic architecture.

facts.fact: Its west front recalls a westwork or the outside of a church organ, and includes a 49-metre bell tower.
facts.quote: The most striking feature of the building is its west façade, reminiscent of a westwork or of the exterior of a church organ. It includes the 49 m (160 ft) tall bell tower.

facts.fact: Some five million yellow bricks were used.
facts.quote: Some five million yellow bricks, a typical Danish building material, were used for the edifice.

facts.fact: Yellow brick and a lack of ornament give Gothic height with a minimal modern look.
facts.quote: But it is the yellow brick and the lack of ornamentation which contribute to the Gothic verticality while adhering to the minimalist modern aesthetic.

facts.fact: The Szczecin Philharmonic, founded in 1948, is the philharmonic of the city of Szczecin, Poland.
facts.quote: Szczecin Philharmonic, officially Mieczysław Karłowicz Philharmonic (Polish: Filharmonia im. Mieczysława Karłowicza), founded in 1948, is a philharmonic of the city of Szczecin, Poland.

facts.fact: Since 14 September 2014 it has been housed in a new building designed by Barozzi Veiga of Barcelona.
facts.quote: From September 14, 2014 the new seat of the Philharmonic is a building on 48 Małopolska Street, designed by Studio Barozzi Veiga from Barcelona.

facts.fact: The 13,000 m² building has a 1,000-seat concert hall and a 200-seat smaller hall.
facts.quote: The music venue covers an area of 13,000 square meters and contains a main concert hall with 1000 seats for concert-goers as well as a smaller hall with a capacity for 200 spectators and a number of conference rooms.

facts.fact: Its ice-like form and translucent ribbed-glass facade, which glows white at night, have made it a new icon of the city.
facts.quote: The characteristic ice-like shape of the philharmonic and its translucent ribbed-glass façade, which gives the building a white glow at night, has become a new icon of the city and has received numerous architectural awards such as First Prize in the prestigious Eurobuild Awards 2014 contest in the category of Architectural Design of the Year.

facts.fact: In 2015 the building won the European Union Prize for Contemporary Architecture.
facts.quote: In 2015, the new building of the philharmonic was awarded the European Union Prize for Contemporary Architecture.

facts.fact: Krzysztof Penderecki composed a fanfare for its opening in 2014.
facts.quote: In 2014, a prominent Polish composer Krzysztof Penderecki specially composed a fanfare for the official opening ceremony of the new building and it was performed by the Szczecin Philharmonic Orchestra.

facts.fact: Ještěd Tower is a television transmitter on top of Mount Ještěd near Liberec, Czech Republic.
facts.quote: Ještěd Tower (Czech: Hotel a televizní vysílač na Ještědu) is a television transmitter on top of Mount Ještěd near Liberec in the Czech Republic.

facts.fact: It is 94 metres tall, made of reinforced concrete in a hyperboloid shape.
facts.quote: Measuring 94 m (308 ft), it is made of reinforced concrete shaped in a "hyperboloid" form.

facts.fact: It was designed by Karel Hubáček, with Zdeněk Patrman on structure and Otakar Binar on the interiors.
facts.quote: The tower was designed by architect Karel Hubáček, who was assisted by Zdeněk Patrman, involved in building statics, and by Otakar Binar, who designed the interior furnishing.

facts.fact: The design took from 1963 to 1966 and construction from 1966 to 1973.
facts.quote: It took the team three years to finalize the structure design (1963–1966). The construction itself took seven years to finish (1966–1973).

facts.fact: The hyperboloid shape extends the silhouette of the hill and resists the extreme weather on the summit.
facts.quote: The hyperboloid shape was chosen since it naturally extends the silhouette of the hill and, moreover, resists the extreme climate conditions on the summit of Mount Ještěd.

facts.fact: It combines a mountain hotel and a TV transmitter, with the hotel and restaurant in its lowest sections.
facts.quote: The design combines the operation of a mountaintop hotel and a television transmitter. The hotel and restaurant are located in the lowest sections of the tower.

facts.fact: In 1969 Hubáček received the Perret Prize of the International Union of Architects.
facts.quote: In 1969, Karel Hubáček was awarded the Perret Prize of the International Union of Architects (UIA).

facts.fact: It has been a national cultural monument since 2006 and has been on UNESCO's Tentative List since 2007.
facts.quote: The tower has been on the list of Czech cultural monuments since 1998, becoming a national cultural monument in 2006. In 2007, it was entered on the Tentative List of UNESCO World Heritage sites.

facts.fact: The IIM Bangalore campus was designed under B. V. Doshi, winner of the 2018 Pritzker Prize.
facts.quote: The design of IIMB campus was led by the famous architect B.V. Doshi, , the 2018 Pritzker Architecture Prize laureate, RIBA 2022 Royal Gold Medal recipient, and Padma Bhushan awardee.

facts.fact: The design drew on the city of Fatehpur Sikri, the Meenakshi Temple in Madurai and Bangalore's gardens.
facts.quote: The design was inspired by the 16th-century historic city of Fatehpur Sikri near Agra, and the 13th-century Meenakshi Temple in Madurai, along with the lush gardens of Bangalore, also known as the Garden City of India.

facts.fact: Light and environment were the basis of its poly-nuclear design, a mix of Indian tradition and Team 10 modernism.
facts.quote: Light and Environment were the cornerstones of the poly-nuclear design, a hybrid of Indian traditional architecture and principles of Team 10 modernists.

facts.fact: It has high passageways, trellises, green open quadrangles, pergolas, semi-open corridors and Kota stone floors.
facts.quote: The notable architectural elements include the high passageways, trellises, open quadrangles with space for greenery, sunlight beaming in through the pergolas, semi-open corridors, geometrical roofs, rough texture finish, and Kota-stone flooring.

facts.fact: The original complex is built of hand-chipped granite masonry and exposed concrete.
facts.quote: The 54,000 sq-m original complex is built of hand-chipped granite stonemasonry, and exposed concrete.

facts.fact: The campus was designed from 1977, and its buildings were finished in 1983.
facts.quote: The campus design began in 1977, and the construction of buildings was finished in 1983.

facts.fact: When Dezeen asked 13 leading Indian firms for their favourite building, IIMB was the only one chosen by more than one firm.
facts.quote: When Dezeen asked thirteen top Indian architecture firms to list their favourite building, IIMB was the only building chosen by more than one, and called it "the most influential piece of (Indian) modern architecture".

facts.fact: The India Habitat Centre is a multipurpose building in New Delhi.
facts.quote: The India Habitat Centre is a multipurpose building in the city of New Delhi, India.

facts.fact: It was started in 1993.
facts.quote: The India Habitat Centre was started in 1993.

facts.fact: HUDCO wanted offices for its staff and invited non-profit groups working on habitat to share the building.
facts.quote: The public agency for the Housing and Urban Development Corporation (HUDCO) wanted an office building for its workers and made the unprecedented decision to invite chosen nonprofit organizations that shared their concern with habitat to share that work space.

facts.fact: HUDCO's chairman Santosh Sharma and the architect Joseph Allen Stein turned the office building into an urban design project.
facts.quote: The chairman of HUDCO Santosh Sharma and the architect Joseph Allen Stein decided to radically change the traditional image of an office building as an architectural project and transformed it into an urban design project.

facts.fact: Members share services inside and out, around multiple courtyards with meeting rooms, a library, restaurants and more.
facts.quote: The space was designed to permit the members of the centre to share services both inside and outside the building with multiple courtyards, common meeting rooms, shared parking area, library, restaurants, museum, and hotels, some of which are open to the general public.

facts.fact: It is divided into five blocks linked by aerial walkways.
facts.quote: Divided into five blocks which are connected with aerial walkaways, IHC can conduct up to 20 concurrent sessions from socio-cultural events and exhibitions to business and economic events.

facts.fact: It occupies nine acres in the city.
facts.quote: Constructed on nine acres in an urban area, the building eschewed traditional building materials and techniques.

facts.fact: The Jantar Mantar is a set of 19 astronomical instruments built by Sawai Jai Singh, the founder of Jaipur.
facts.quote: The Jantar Mantar is a collection of 19 astronomical instruments built by the Rajput king Sawai Jai Singh, the founder of Jaipur, Rajasthan, India.

facts.fact: It was completed in 1734.
facts.quote: The monument was completed in 1734.

facts.fact: It has the world's largest stone sundial and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.quote: It features the world's largest stone sundial, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

facts.fact: The instruments allow positions in the sky to be observed with the naked eye.
facts.quote: The instruments allow the observation of astronomical positions with the naked eye.

facts.fact: The instruments are built of local stone and marble, with scales marked on the marble linings.
facts.quote: Built from local stone and marble, each instrument carries an astronomical scale, generally marked on the marble inner lining.

facts.fact: The Vrihat Samrat Yantra, the "great king of instruments", is 27 metres high.
facts.quote: The Vrihat Samrat Yantra, which means the "great king of instruments", is 88 feet (27 m) high, making it one of the world's largest sundials.

facts.fact: Its face is angled at 27 degrees, the latitude of Jaipur.
facts.quote: Its face is angled at 27 degrees, the latitude of Jaipur.

facts.fact: UNESCO calls it the most significant and best-preserved historic observatory in India.
facts.quote: UNESCO describes the observatory as the most significant and best-preserved historic observatory in India, representing the astronomical and cosmological knowledge of ancient India.
